Hi Sanjay — great to hear. We can accommodate most of these asks; pushing a couple of clarifications below so we align the draft correctly:

1) Failover semantics: Are you asking for automatic cross-region failover with transparent request routing, or a documented manual failover process with a 15 minute warmup for stateful workloads?
2) Latency targets: Is the p95/p99 defined for user-facing single-request latency (end-to-end including network) or per-token server-side latency? We typically commit server-side per-token and provide observed E2E numbers as guidance.
3) Billing/credits: We can propose a degradation credit schedule for availability and a separate uplift/adjustment when model-variant fallbacks are used. Would you prefer credits on a monthly invoice or a one-time pro-rated credit?

I’ll loop in Karthik to draft redlines to the order form and Monica for the evidence bundle (SOC2 excerpts + failover runbook). We’ll aim to get a first pass to you by EOD Friday.

Cheers,

Hi all — attached are the redlines and the draft order-form SLA rider. Key points in this draft:

- Failover: We define two modes (Automatic Stateles Routing; Manual Stateful Escalation). Automatic routing will attempt transparent cross-region routing for stateless inference requests; we explicitly carve out short cache-warmup windows (we commit to notifying Biocare within 5 minutes of failover start).
- Latency commitments: We commit to server-side per-token latency: p95 < 130ms, p99 < 350ms for dedicated capacity. We include an optional tighter p95 (120ms) as an addendum contingent on a dedicated burst reservation (detailed in order form).
- Fallback & credits: If a fallback to a lower-capacity model variant or alternate region occurs, Redwood will apply a 10% billing adjustment for the affected billing cycle and provide a post-incident report within 7 days. Availability credits follow the banded schedule Rachel proposed.
- Evidence bundle: Monica has attached SOC2 excerpts and a 2-page failover runbook (see attachment list).
